title: Positive-signature compact 2D scalar eigenmode benchmark
metric: ds6^2=e^(2A(theta)) g_mn dx^m dx^n + R^2[dtheta^2+beta^2 sin^2(theta)dchi^2]
sector: axisymmetric scalar modes m_chi=0 on a positive-definite compact internal two-space

sturm_liouville.equation: -d/dtheta[p f_n'] + q f_n = lambda_n w f_n
sturm_liouville.normalization: integral dtheta dchi exp(2A) sqrt(g2) f_n f_m = delta_nm

overlap.minimal_zero_mode_theorem: for mu_6=0 and natural/Neumann boundary conditions on a connected compact domain, f_0 is constant and xi_0=1
overlap.consequence: warping alone changes the normalization weight and warped volume but not the coordinate profile of the exact minimal zero mode

exact_sphere_control.eigenfunctions: axisymmetric spherical harmonics proportional to P_l(cos theta)

interpretation.secured_result: the exact massless Neumann zero mode of the minimal scalar branch is constant and cannot provide the large brane enhancement required by the 0.5 natural benchmark
interpretation.nonminimal_options: bulk mass, position-dependent kinetic functions, brane kinetic terms or Robin interactions may alter the lightest profile but must be checked for nonzero mass, tachyons, ghosts and consistency with the parent action
interpretation.not_a_global_no_go: the result blocks warp-only localization of the minimal scalar zero mode, not every possible higher-dimensional baryogenesis operator

limitations: the background warp profile and cap geometry are benchmark inputs rather than solutions of COS-02.2B
only the axisymmetric scalar sector is solved
metric, flux, radion and scalar perturbations are not mixed
brane kinetic terms and position-dependent Z_6 are not included
the Ritz solver is a low-dimensional diagnostic, not a spectral proof for arbitrary singular backgrounds
no evidence effect; K1-D and K1-E remain closed
